A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same neural operator splitting work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original PDE prediction experiments, parameter-recovery results, compute-scaling measurements and an operator-accuracy analysis in Section 5 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds robustness tests, mixed-physics training experiments, ablations, sensitivity studies and runtime measurements in Appendices C.2–C.7.

M1.justification: The DISCO dictionary construction, search objective, uniform and beam searches, and Lie/Strang splitting procedures remain unchanged. The new training ablations test existing components; they do not replace the proposed method.

E1.justification: The four primary PDE benchmarks remain. Coverage expands within advection–diffusion through an unseen Burgers-like perturbation and mixed-physics training followed by joint coefficient extrapolation (C.2–C.3). Both versions already contain seven main composition tasks; the revised task count is a textual correction.

E2.justification: FNO is added as an evaluated comparator in both composition and parameter-extrapolation comparisons, with results in Tables 1–2. MPP, Zebra, GEPS and direct DISCO remain. The added SINDy discussion does not constitute an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The main evaluation settings are retained, but substantial new protocols are introduced: seven perturbation strengths with 128 trajectories each and 84-step rollouts, mixed-training proportions, controlled retraining ablations, dictionary-size and fitting-window sweeps, and per-sample A100 timing (C.2–C.7). The GEPS adaptation budgets of 100/500/2000 steps were already documented in v1.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained operator-quality analysis and qualitative rollouts, v2 tests missing dictionary physics, entangled training operators, dependence on in-context conditioning and the codebook, sensitivity to dictionary size and observation length, and accuracy versus adaptation time. These directly investigate robustness, component contributions and practical efficiency.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new trajectory counts describe evaluation samples, and GEPS optimization lengths do not establish additional independent repetitions.

E6.justification: Existing entries in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. v2 adds FNO scores and Tables 4–9, including Navier–Stokes error of 0.563 without the codebook versus 0.066 with it, and beam-search error rising from 0.055 to 0.797 as the unseen perturbation increases. These are new experimental comparisons, not changed performance under the original settings. Section 5.3 also corrects '5 out of 6' to '6 out of 7'.

T1.justification: The formal PDE-family setup, search objective, splitting formulas and stated accuracy orders are retained. No new theorem, proof or substantive theoretical derivation is added; the new perturbation equation specifies an empirical stress test.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central zero-shot generalization, compositional search and parameter-recovery claims. The conclusion adds a claim that search overhead is competitive with gradient-based fine-tuning in the reported 1D/2D experiments, extending the claim of computational practicality.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands applicability and failure analysis. It interprets diffusion-estimation bias under missing physics, argues that sufficiently diverse coupled dictionaries can work without pure-physics training, and identifies the training recipe as complementary to search. It also qualifies short-window robustness by dynamics and adds search overhead and possible 3D bottlenecks to the limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code repository link, detailed FNO architecture and training settings, A100 hardware information, and disclosures about dictionary selection and Navier–Stokes codebook use. These are targeted reproducibility additions. B.4's assertion that FNO budgets match MPP conflicts with its retained MPP description, so matching budgets cannot be confirmed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Sergeant-Perthuis et al. to the symmetry discussion and relates parameter recovery to SINDy, distinguishing learned-operator search from symbolic sparse regression. The added Li et al. 2021 reference describes the same FNO work already cited as Li et al. 2020, rather than a distinct research contribution.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section organization remain intact. Changes include targeted explanations and corrections, appendix subsections and cross-references, a clarification about compatible backbones, and updated affiliations, acknowledgements and publication text.

P2.justification: Tables 4–9 substantially expand the presentation with robustness, ablation, sensitivity and accuracy/time displays; Tables 1–2 gain FNO rows. The scaling-law plot moves and becomes Figure 4 instead of Figure 3, while Figure 2 and Table 3 receive clearer captions. Existing plot data and qualitative images are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendices C.2–C.7 address central gaps in v1 concerning training restrictions, component contributions and adaptation cost. Coupled-only training still benefits from search (direct NRMSE 0.278 versus beam 0.190), while removing the Navier–Stokes codebook raises error from 0.066 to 0.563, clarifying an important dependency. Together with failure and runtime analyses, this substantially strengthens the empirical support and applicability boundaries. The new FNO/MPP budget inconsistency and continued absence of uncertainty estimates limit precision but do not outweigh these gains.
